name: Stumm
kurzbeschreibung: A historic gem in the Zillertal, featuring Schloss Stumm and the late Gothic church—a true treasure of Tirol’s past.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Stumm is situated at an elevation of 550 meters in the central Zillertal within the district of Schwaz, set upon the sunny eastern banks of the river Ziller directly opposite Kaltenbach. Home to approximately 1,910 residents, this historic village is celebrated as one of the architectural and cultural jewels of the valley. The heart of Stumm is its historic village square, exceptional in its completeness and picturesque charm, often chosen as a setting for television and film productions. Framed by ascending mountain pastures, the rushing Märzenbach torrent, and the Kitzbühel Alps, Stumm combines authentic village serenity and vibrant artistic traditions with immediate access to premier alpine recreation.

Geschichte

The settlement history of Stumm extends back to the early medieval era. As early as the 8th century, Duke Tassilo III of Bavaria gifted estates in Stumm to the monastery of Herrenchiemsee. The village was first officially documented as Stume in 1143. For centuries, the community served as the administrative core of the Hofmark Stumm. A major turning point occurred in 1556 when the renowned Innsbruck cannon and bell founder Gregor Löffler acquired the estate and constructed the Renaissance manor Schloss Stumm, complete with four corner oriels and a hipped roof. The property later passed to the Counts of Lodron, whose heraldic coat of arms still adorns the main portal. The parish church dedicated to Saint Rupert highlights a historic diocesan border: from the 8th century onward, the river Ziller divided the bishoprics of Salzburg and Brixen. Consecrated in 1511 in late Gothic style, the church was lavishly expanded in 1765 with Rococo ornamentation, featuring celebrated ceiling frescoes by Christoph Anton Mayr depicting the life of Saint Rupert and exquisite stucco work by Anton Gigl.

Anreise

Traveling to Stumm is straightforward by car and public transport. Drivers exit the Inntalautobahn A12 at Wiesing/Zillertal and follow the B169 Zillertalstraße up the valley to the Kaltenbach/Stumm exit, crossing the river bridge directly into the village center. Toll-free access from Bavaria is available via Lake Tegernsee or the Achen Pass. Rail travelers arrive via the major junction of Jenbach, transferring to the scenic Zillertalbahn to the Kaltenbach-Stumm station. From there, an easy 500-meter walk across the bridge brings visitors right onto the village square. Regular VVT bus line 8330 and local winter ski shuttles provide seamless transit throughout the region.

Tipps

A leisurely stroll across the historic village square, taking in Schloss Stumm, the parish church, and the heritage fountain bearing the statue of Saint Florian, offers an enchanting journey into Tyrolean history. In summer, the acclaimed cultural festival stummer schrei draws art enthusiasts from near and far, staging contemporary theater, literature, and music in the festival barn and open-air venues. Families and swimmers relish the Badewelt Stumm leisure complex with its natural swimming pond, water slides, and lap pools. Hikers can embark on refreshing walks into the romantic Märzenklamm gorge or head to the nearby Hochzillertal-Kaltenbach cable car terminal in winter.
